question: A Mallampati Class IV airway (only hard palate visible on examination) predicts a higher likelihood of difficult direct laryngoscopy compared with a Mallampati Class I airway.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Mallampati Class IV does indicate greater predicted difficulty. As the Mallampati class increases from I to IV, the view at laryngoscopy tends to worsen (Cormack-Lehane grade worsens), signalling potential for difficult intubation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Mallampati Class IV (hard palate alone visible) correlates with restricted mouth opening and limited oropharyngeal space, increasing the likelihood of a Cormack-Lehane Grade III or IV view at laryngoscopy.
